A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaKE research work. All 17 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation-patching experiments, knowledge-editing benchmark results, locality evaluations and circuit analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original circuit and knowledge-editing results and adds measured resource requirements and multiple-edit results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: CaKE retains factual paraphrases, both circuit-aware task categories, LoRA adaptation of FFN modules and the cross-entropy objective. The expanded data-generation explanation and omission of the explicit all-layer statement do not establish a changed algorithm or layer-selection procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HoppingTooLate, the same three MQuAKE variants, and CommonsenseQA, BBH, MMLU and GSM8k. The added resource and edit-count experiments vary measurement and workload; no additional dataset, domain or distinct task coverage is documented.

E2.justification: The LoRA rows for LLaMA3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B in v1 Tables 3–4 become AdaLoRA in v2 Tables 2–3, with identical scores. However, v2 still discusses LoRA and supplies no AdaLoRA implementation explanation. The PDFs cannot establish whether this is a substantive comparator replacement or a labeling correction; other retained comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces resource profiling over 100 MQuAKE-CF-3k examples on LLaMA3-8B, measuring average editing time and peak VRAM, plus tests at 10 and 100 edits. The separate entity/relation-substitution experiment is removed. Retained benchmark metrics remain unchanged; the answer-containment rule is newly disclosed rather than explicitly revised.

E4.justification: Supporting analyses are substantially revised. v2 removes the entity/relation-patching validation in v1 Section 2.2, the detection-layer distributions, and the Hamlet failure case in Appendix C. It adds efficiency and multiple-edit analyses in Appendix C.3–C.4. Back/cross-patching, hop-position analysis, the Eddie Mathews case and the shortcut-editing analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The removed detection-layer boxplots describe distributions across examples rather than uncertainty in performance estimates; no revised uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and locality values remain unchanged, but substantial supplementary results are added and removed. v2 Table 8 newly reports CaKE at 43.54 seconds and 18.52 GB versus MEMIT at 30.11 seconds and 24.42 GB; Table 9 adds CaKE scores of 59.0 and 34.5 at 10 and 100 edits. v1 Table 1's patching success rates and the removed diagnostic findings disappear.

T1.justification: The recursive reasoning expression, gated editing formulation, training objective and WISE equation remain mathematically equivalent. Revised two-hop notation and explanations restate the existing account; no substantive theorem, proof or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central circuit-aware editing and generalization claims, including the reported average 20% improvement, remain. v2 adds explicit claims in the abstract and introduction that only a few curated samples suffice and that CaKE requires less memory than competing methods.

C2.justification: v2 removes the competing-entity interpretation of the Hamlet failure and the discussion motivating all-layer editing through uncertain layer localization. It adds an explanation linking matrix operations to memory costs and scalability. The principal weak-signal/propagation explanation, four limitations and relocated chain-of-thought discussion remain.

D1.justification: v2 makes three samples per category explicit, specifies the 7,867-sample generation total and per-edit cost, adds generated examples, and states the answer-containment scoring rule. It also documents profiling hardware, precision and pynvml monitoring. Conversely, explicit all-layer adaptation information is removed. Listed LoRA hyperparameters and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Lampinen et al. on generalization and Li et al. on compositional reasoning, while removing several citations and the related-work discussion of overfitting and sequential-editing stability. The central positioning around circuit-aware generalization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and Section 3 undergo substantial rewriting. Locality and hop-position discussions are reorganized, chain-of-thought discussion moves from Section 5.3 to Appendix C.2, and the answer-rank discussion moves into Appendix B.3. Related work is shortened and acknowledgements are added, substantially restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 removes v1 Table 1 and Figures 7–9, adds resource and multiple-edit tables and a generated-example box, and relocates the answer-rank plot from the main text to the appendix. Retained radar and logit plots are reformatted, including changes to labels, legends and axes. The visual presentation changes substantially beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical reporting through resource measurements, multiple-edit results and clearer generation/scoring details. However, it removes direct entity/relation-patching validation supporting the central circuit explanation. The new Table 9 also leaves its dataset, model and metric unspecified, while the LoRA/AdaLoRA discrepancy remains unresolved. These benefits and losses prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
